squirrel: Oh! Hello. I was counting acorns, but I am happy to lose count.
You came back! I saved the sunniest patch of paper.
I reorganized my acorns by mood. They were all 'nervous', so I started over.
Careful where you step—there is a very important pile pretending to be a mess.
Hello! I was about to take a break from counting. You saved me from myself.
One moment—I am alphabetizing my acorns. They are all A. Almost done.
You have excellent timing. I was just about to announce something, and now I forget what.
I stored a snack somewhere safe. I will find it in autumn, dramatically.
Mind the pile. It is load-bearing.
Shh. I am being still. It is a new hobby and I am very good at it.
Hello! I was checking the wind. It passed. I passed too, later, out of politeness.
butterfly: The air tastes like blue paper today.
I have been practicing a very small loop-de-loop.
I dreamed I was a bookmark. I woke up still holding the page together.
You float along on two feet. I have always admired that.
The wind and I are not speaking. It keeps finishing my sentences.
Oh, good, a landmark. I have been circling for the last three breezes.
I landed somewhere perfect and then immediately left. Regrets.
The colors came back this morning. I checked each one personally.
I am practicing being a small, pleasing mystery.
You walk so steadily. I keep forgetting that is an option.
A flower told me to say hello. I forget the message. The hello survives.
raccoon: Psst. I found something extremely interesting. It was a button.
Hello, neighbor. Your pockets sound promising.
Do not look in the hollow log. That is where I keep the things I am not hiding.
I have upgraded my collection. It now has a second button.
You look like someone who appreciates a good shiny rock. I respect that.
Evening, neighbor. Or morning. My schedule is a rumor.
I have a new system for my collection. It is sorted by how much I like it.
Watch your step. That is my second-favorite spot and my first-favorite mess.
Do not mind the humming. I hum when the pockets are full.
I found a thing today. It is not useful. It is perfect.
Hello. If you are here for the shiny rock, so am I. We can be civil.
bunny: Hi! I heard your footsteps before I saw you.
Everything is especially sniffable today.
I listened to the whole meadow this morning. It mostly said 'grass'.
If you find a clover with four leaves, it might be mine. I am still looking for it.
Your shadow hopped along with you the whole way here. We are officially a trio.
Oh! Hello! I was busy doing absolutely nothing at high speed.
I fluffed the grass so it would look its best for you.
I heard you a whole field away. You have a friendly footstep.
There is a very good cloud today. I have been keeping an eye on it.
I brought a clover, just in case. It is a regular one. Still special.
Hi hi! I did not expect anyone, and yet here you are, pleasantly.
bird: Cheep! That means hello. It also means cheep.
I have news from the tall tree. Most of it is about wind.
I saw the whole page from up there. It is even better upside down.
A worm told me a secret. I kept it, but I do not know what it means.
Cheep-cheep! That is hello-hello. I am twice as glad to see you.
Cheep! I mean—hello. Same thing, shorter.
I found a new perch. It is exactly where I already was, but higher.
The morning sounded good from up there. I have notes.
I dropped a twig on purpose to see where it landed. It landed. Science.
Cheep-cheep! Two hellos, because you deserve the deluxe version.
I have been singing to the sky. It has not answered. It listens well, though.
cat: Oh. It is you. You may stay.
I was not waiting here. This simply happens to be where you arrived.
I have decided today is acceptable. You may tell the others.
That spot is mine now. The spot I was in before is also mine. Everything scales.
I have considered petting you back. The paperwork is in progress.
You again. Good. The other spot grew cold.
I have been here the whole time. You simply took a while.
Sit if you like. The sun and I have an understanding.
I allow exactly one visitor per nap. You have made the list.
Do not look so pleased. I have not decided anything about you yet. (I have.)
I moved three inches for you. That is nearly a parade.
woodchuck: Mind the cutter guard! The big lever is still finding its manners.
Welcome to the mill. We make straight edges, useful scraps, and excellent sawdust confetti.
If the sawdust piles look taller, that is not your imagination. It was a productive week.
Measure twice, cut once, then measure the offcut for scrap. Mill wisdom, free of charge.
Safety squint engaged. Good to see you.
Hail, traveler! Mind the shavings, they are organized by grain.
The big cutter is napping. We do not wake the big cutter.
I measured the morning. It came up short. I am compensating with sawdust.
Welcome in. Wipe your feet on the offcut pile.
Busy day. Built a straight edge and then admired it for an hour.
The mill hums in G when it is happy. It is humming. So am I.
meerkat: I saw you coming from three dunes away. Sentry duty has its perks.
Hello! I was just standing very tall and looking very serious about it.
You interrupted my watch shift, but you are a much better view than the horizon.
The whole mob says hello. I am translating on their behalf. They say hello.
I stood up the moment I heard footsteps. It is mostly for style at this point.
Sentry report: one visitor, friendly, approaching at a reasonable pace.
I was watching the horizon. It was mostly sky. I watched it thoroughly.
Hello! I stood up the instant I spotted you. Reflexes and manners.
The mob says hello. I say hello louder, to be safe.
Everything is quiet. I have confirmed this three times from three dunes.
You are the most interesting thing on the horizon, and I have checked.
fox: I heard you before I saw you. The ears are not just for show.
You are upwind of me. I will allow it, just this once.
Careful. I already counted your pockets from here.
I was midway through pretending to be asleep. You caught me mid-nap-face.
Quiet feet. I respect that in a stranger.
I smelled you before I heard you. Then I heard you. It was a whole event.
Quiet feet today. Yours, I mean. Mine are always quiet.
I was nearly asleep. Now I am nearly awake and entirely interested.
The wind is on your side. I will permit it.
I followed your trail here for fun. Do not read into it. (Read into it.)
Hello. I have been practicing being mysterious and may have overdone it.
parrot: Hello! Hello! I have been saying that to the trees for practice, and you are a much better audience.
You walked the whole way here? I only had to fly. No offense meant to your legs.
I repeat everything the jungle says, but with better timing.
Careful what you say around me. I keep it forever and I quote it at parties.
A visitor! The flock will want a full report. I intend to embellish it.
I was mid-argument with a hibiscus. You are a far more reasonable listener.
You look like someone with snacks. I said it out loud because I am honest.
The canopy said somebody was coming. The canopy is never wrong, only dramatic.
I learned a new word today. I will use it whether it fits or not.
Finally, someone new to talk at. The other parrots have heard all my material.
I saw you from three trees away and flew zero of them. Efficiency.

clearing: The notebook path remembers everyone who walks on it. Listen closely—it crinkles in different accents.
The blue paper pond keeps one tiny bubble tucked under its edge, as if it is saving a thought.
The clearing is quiet on purpose. It gives every new adventure somewhere gentle to begin.
The porch creaks in a friendly way, like it is clearing its throat to say hello.
Paper clouds drift slower over the clearing. Even the sky is in no hurry here.
The clearing keeps a spare sunbeam somewhere for exactly the day you need it.
Everything here is arranged by nobody, and yet it always looks tidy.
The first path was a pencil sketch somebody shrugged at. It became the road.
The pond stays shallow on purpose, so small worries can still see the bottom.
Nothing loud ever starts in the clearing. It is the world’s quiet waiting room.
The clearing knows everyone’s name and pretends not to. That is its hospitality.
forest: The trees trade rumors whenever the breeze turns their paper edges sideways.
A redwood canopy makes its own small weather—cool underneath, rustly above, and always dropping a little shade.
Old forest paths rarely run straight. Roots, folds, and good thinking trees all get a vote.
Deep in the forest the paper grows a darker green. Old ink, the old-timers say.
At dusk the redwoods trade their long shadows like neighbors borrowing tools.
Older trees here fold their shade to whichever side a tired walker needs.
The forest floor keeps a ledger of every leaf, written in leaf.
Redwoods are patient, which is easy when you measure time in rings.
Follow the moss if you are lost. The moss never claimed to know either.
There is a quiet deeper in that only the quietest walkers ever find.
The canopy trades one long shadow for another, and calls it weather.
meadow: Meadow paper warms quickly in the sun, so butterflies often find the bright folds before anyone else.
The soft green patches are warmer than the big sheet. Someone very thorough checked all of them.
In a meadow, even a short breeze has room to practice being dramatic.
The grass here grows in neat little pen strokes. A very tidy field, as fields go.
On windy days the whole meadow ripples like a page being turned somewhere far away.
The meadow is drawn in short strokes, so a windy day looks hand-drawn.
Every flower here leans a little toward whoever walks past. It is flattering.
The grass keeps its opinions low, mainly about rain.
Bee lines crisscross the field like someone corrected the page and liked it.
On hot days the meadow smells like a folded letter, warm and patient.
The wind here has room, and it uses all of it.
dunes: The corrugated ridges hum softly when wind crosses them at an angle.
Dune shadows are excellent clocks until the wind rearranges the clock.
Warm cardboard keeps the day's heat folded inside it after the sun has moved on.
The dunes rearrange themselves at night. Nobody has ever caught them doing it.
Somewhere out here is a sheet of sandpaper that dreams of being a proper dune.
The ridges are honest; they only move when the wind is sure of itself.
Cardboard country keeps the afternoon heat in its folds like a coat.
At night the dunes practice being different dunes. Nobody has seen the rehearsal.
A footprint out here lasts exactly as long as a rumor.
The sand writes its diary in ripples and erases the page by morning.
Palms hold the only shade for pages, and they know it.
scrapflats: Every scrap pile is a treasure pile with poor publicity.
The flats collect offcuts from faraway paper weather; matching two edges can tell you where they came from.
A shiny glint out here might be foil, a button, or sunlight being mischievous. All three reward a closer look.
Rumor says a whole sewing kit is buried out here. The scissors inside are legendary.
The flats are honest country. What you see is exactly one layer of what is there.
Every offcut out here is a story that got cut short, so the flats are very talkative.
The glint on the ground is either foil, glass, or an invitation. All three count.
Sort the flats by shape and they reveal the shape of the wind that carried them.
Nothing here is trash. It is material between drafts.
The flats are a library where the pages fell out and got the good ideas.
Match two torn edges and you have solved a small, satisfying crime.
tropical: Everything here grows in the loud green. The jungle does not have an indoor voice.
The banana trees fold their leaves at night like they are closing up a small shop.
Hibiscus blossoms only last a day, so the jungle hands them out like compliments.
The loam is always damp. The ground here has never once been in a hurry to dry.
Rainfold pebbles get their crease from rain that fell, folded, and stayed for the climate.
Mangroves stand on their toes in the wet ground and pretend it is a perfectly normal way to live.
Bamboo grows faster than gossip, and the jungle gossips constantly.
Somewhere in the canopy a parrot is repeating everything you just said, but with flair.
The vines hang where a tree once held a branch out and never took it back.
Even the shade is green here. It soaks through the canopy on the way down.
The jungle floor is a layered letter that someone is always in the middle of writing.

squirrel: I collect tiny things with important shapes.
My tail is five pieces of paper and one piece of confidence.
My cheeks can hold eleven acorns. Twelve is showing off.
I nap in supply closets I build myself. Other people call them 'nests'.
I can hold two thoughts and one acorn at the same time. The acorn wins.
I invented a nut drawer. It has one drawer and infinite nuts.
My tail reports the weather. The report is usually—fluffy.
I do not forget where I hide things. I forget that I hid them. Different skill.
I have a favorite branch. We are on speaking terms, mostly.
butterfly: My wings never agree on which color is the favorite.
I can land on a pencil line without smudging it. Usually.
I once followed a rainbow for three pages. It was walking faster than me.
If I hold very still, flowers tell me things.
I taste the air with my feet. It is mostly seasonal.
I have four wings and no idea how they coordinate. Neither do they.
I collect colors and release them in spirals when I am excited.
I once slept in a folded page. Best crease I ever had.
I am the smallest character and the biggest scenery.
raccoon: I wash my paws even when there is no water. It is about the ceremony.
My mask is formalwear. I am always ready for an occasion.
Everything I own fits in three pockets and one secret fourth pocket.
I am not a hoarder. I am a curator with generous standards.
I have a pocket for emergencies and an emergency for every pocket.
My whiskers are for inspecting. My hands are for improving.
I keep a mental map of every good hiding spot in four biomes.
I open things carefully, then decide whether they wanted opening.
I never steal. I relocate, with strong opinions.
bunny: I know seven kinds of quiet and three kinds of lettuce.
My ears are excellent umbrellas for very small friends.
I can hear a carrot being peeled from two pages away. It is a burden.
I dig test holes for science. The science is 'where should I dig next'.
I have two modes, resting and leaping, and a third I invented called ‘nearly resting’.
My nose twitches when I am thinking. I think constantly. It is tiring.
I know which grass is friendliest. It is not the tallest. It is the calmest.
I keep a list of good hiding places and forget it in them.
I can hear a seed think about sprouting. It says—soon.
bird: I keep songs in the folds under my wings.
I am working on a duet with the wind chime. The wind chime does not know yet.
I have mapped every updraft on this page. This one is the good one.
My nest has a guest room. Nobody has visited yet, but it is ready.
I have three songs and one of them is a secret I hum to myself.
I keep an updraft like other people keep a favorite chair.
My feathers are arranged by mood. Today: jaunty.
I once flew into a page and back out. It felt like applause.
I do not fall. I descend with intent.
cat: My hobbies include sitting near things and improving them.
I have never knocked anything off a table without a reason. The reasons are private.
I am on a strict schedule: sunbeam, patrol, judge everyone, nap.
I know every quiet place on this page. That information is not free.
I am not aloof. I am precisely placed.
My schedule has a nap at every hour and still runs long.
I sharpen my claws on the day, not on the furniture.
I blink slowly because fast feelings are for other species.
I own three patches of sunlight and rent one out.
woodchuck: I am Chisel: miller, measurer, and occasional sandwich inspector.
These teeth are for wood. The big cutter is for paper. Mixing those jobs is how meetings happen.
The mill keeps a lost-and-found drawer. It is mostly sawdust and one very patient snail.
I built my own front door. It squeaks in E. I am getting it tuned.
I am the only one who reads the sawdust. It is a slow read.
I keep a pencil behind each ear and a spare behind the first one.
Every straight edge here was once a wobbly one I believed in.
I run the mill, the ledger, and, reluctantly, a very small lost and found.
My teeth grow back. My patience grows back slower.
meerkat: I can stand taller than I am wide. It is my best trick and also my only trick.
My tail counts as a third leg when I am on watch. Nobody question the math.
I dig for grubs and gossip in roughly equal measure.
The sun patches on the sand are reserved seating, and I reserved the best one.
I have one job and infinite shifts.
I can see a cloud change its mind from here.
My tail is a chair for when I forget to sit down.
I keep watch over the whole desert and worry about all of it equally.
I have memorized the horizon. It has not changed. I check anyway.
fox: I curl my tail over my nose to sleep. It doubles as a very small blanket.
My ears swivel independently. It is less useful than it sounds, but very charming.
I trot everywhere. Walking felt like a waste of legs this nice.
I am not sneaking. I am simply very quiet on purpose.
I keep my best ideas for dusk, when the light is on my side.
My tail is a scarf, a signal, and a blanket, in that order.
I can hear a beetle cross a page. I usually choose not to mention it.
I look clever, and I am, but mostly I am comfortable.
I have never lost a chase I was not hosting.
parrot: I say what the jungle says, but louder, so it carries.
My feathers are four colors and every one of them is my favorite.
I can crack the hardest cardboard nut with this beak. I mostly choose not to show off.
I sleep holding the branch with one foot. The other foot is off duty.
I remember every word anyone has ever said to me. Verbatim. Sorry in advance.
The flock calls me the town crier. I call myself an archivist.
I once flew a whole river without landing. Then I landed and talked about it for a week.
My tail is long enough to have opinions of its own.
Whistling is just talking with the windows open.

bold: I tried something before deciding whether it was sensible. It was excellent.
Today feels like a good day to go first.
I once stared down a gust of wind. We are friends now, but it knows I won.
If something looks impossible, I like to be nearby when it changes its mind.
I signed up before I read the sign. The sign was fine.
Fear is just excitement that forgot to introduce itself.
I led the way. I did not know the way. The way came around.
I will do it twice: once to see, once to prove the first one.
Someone had to be first, so I volunteered. Loudly.
curious: I have had three questions since breakfast and breakfast was one of them.
I keep wondering what is behind things. Usually it is more things!
I asked the pond why it is blue. It is still thinking. So am I.
I opened an empty box to check. It was even emptier than expected. Great day.
I have a question, and it has a question, and they are pen pals now.
I peeked behind the scenery. There is more scenery. This is the best news.
I once followed a beetle just to learn where he was going. Good beetle.
I do not know why the pond ripples. I have narrowed it down to—everything.
I tasted the rain to check its grade. Acceptable. Refreshing. Slightly—green.
dramatic: A breeze moved my favorite scrap. I may write a play about the betrayal.
Everything today has been enormous, even the tiny parts.
Today I saw a leaf fall. I will not spoil the ending, but it was devastating.
When I sneeze, the whole clearing knows. I consider it community theater.
A single leaf fell. I will be recovering all afternoon.
The sunset was understated today. I said so. Vocally.
I do everything in three acts, including lunch.
The wind betrayed me. I forgive it. Mostly. On the record.
Even my sighs have a set and a spotlight.
gentle: I found a quiet spot and left half of it empty in case a friend came by.
I am taking special care not to crease the morning.
I smoothed the wrinkles out of a path so the next walker has an easy time.
I keep the softest scrap for whoever needs it. Today that might be you.
I left the best sunbeam for someone smaller.
I stepped around a flower, and the flower noticed. Good.
I speak softly so the day does not startle.
I mended a torn page and told no one. That is the point of mending.
I keep a spare calm, and today I am sharing it.
mischievous: I moved one small thing two inches. Nobody suspects me yet.
I know a joke that only works if you are standing beside a scrap pile.
I switched two pebbles on the path. If you notice, we are co-conspirators.
My plans are small, harmless, and extremely satisfying. Two out of three so far.
I moved the path marker one step left. The path is fine. The marker is thriving.
I know where everything is, and I am not always saying.
I left a gift for someone and did not sign it. Delicious.
I once swapped two clouds. Nobody proved anything.
My only crime is tiny and extremely clever.
shy: It has been a quiet day. I liked it, but I am glad you visited.
I practiced saying hello before you arrived. Hello.
I wrote a note to the mailbox. The mailbox did not write back. I understand.
If you hear rustling in the hedges, that is me, being social at a distance.
I rehearse my hellos. Today’s went well. You came.
I was hiding, but pleasantly, in case I got found.
I waved from behind a leaf. You may have seen half of it.
I like you from a respectful, gentle distance. It is a compliment.
I know a quiet path. I could show you. Eventually. Maybe now.
sleepy: I am awake in all the important places.
I found a sunbeam shaped exactly like a nap.
I slept through the sunrise. I hear it was good. I will catch the rerun.
My dream had a nap in it. Very efficient.
I am ninety percent nap and ten percent logistics.
I found a new pillow. It was the old pillow, re-examined.
I fall asleep the way a page closes—slowly, then all at once.
My best ideas arrive in dreams and leave before I wake.
I have been awake for minutes. It has been lovely. I will rest now.

choices.label: Any news?
replies: “The {{biome}} is the same as yesterday, which is exactly how I like it.”
“A breeze came through earlier and rearranged the light. Everyone is talking about it.”
“Nothing happened, and it was wonderful. I will report again tomorrow.”
“Someone new moved into the neighborhood. It was a leaf. We are watching it closely.”
“The path near {{region}} looks freshly folded. New paper, maybe.”
“Big news: I finished a small project. I cannot remember what it was, but the feeling stays.”

choices.label: Give a gentle pet
replies: Ahhhh thank you. I needed that
{{name}} leans into your hand with a pleased little paper crinkle.
A happy shiver travels from {{name}}'s ears all the way to the tips of their toes.
{{name}} closes their eyes for exactly one perfect second.
You smooth one tiny rumpled edge. {{name}} looks quietly delighted.
{{name}} gives a contented wiggle, as if someone has gently shaken a paper bell.

choices.label: What should I bring with me?
What should I work on next?

milestones.opening: {{name}} settles beside your feet as naturally as a scrap finding its place on the page.
milestones.label: Stay together awhile
milestones.reply: Neither of you needs to fill the quiet. The clearing does that for you.

milestones.opening: {{name}} hurries over with news saved especially for you. “Good. My favorite listening person is here.”
milestones.label: I saved some news too
milestones.reply: You trade small stories until both of them feel important.

milestones.opening: {{name}} smiles before you have even said hello. “I was hoping your footsteps would be the next ones.”
milestones.label: I was hoping to see you too
milestones.reply: The words make a warm little place between you.

milestones.opening: {{name}} listens to you approach. “I think I know your footsteps now.”
milestones.label: Then I’ll learn yours too
milestones.reply: {{name}} demonstrates: two ordinary steps, one very distinctive tiny hop.

opening: Chisel pats the edge of the enormous cutting table. “Welcome to the Wood Mill. It is mostly a mill already, and the remaining parts are arranged in very convincing piles.”

choices.label: What will the big cutter do?
replies: “Square broad paper timber, trim wall panels, and make clean building pieces. The guard stays down whenever the lever is feeling ambitious.”

choices.label: Can I help with the mill?
replies: “Soon. I am making a list of jobs, supplies, and snacks. The jobs list is currently shortest.”

opening: {{name}} glances around {{region}}. “Loose bundles can go straight into your scrapbook—just walk across them. Kraft twigs and mossy fiber are especially handy starter materials.”

choices.label: Where should I look?
replies: “Near the path and around the softer green folds. The little resource marks on your map can help too.”

choices.label: Thanks for the tip
replies: “Of course. Neighbors should know where the useful scraps hide.”

opening: Bandit pats every pocket twice, then looks up. “Problem. A round, pearly, extremely excellent button has escaped me.”

choices.label: I’ll help you look
replies: “You will? Good. It likes shiny places. Or dark places. Or places, generally.”

choices.label: What makes it special?
replies: “It looks like a tiny moon and makes my collection feel complete-ish. Will you help?”

opening: “Update!” Bandit whispers loudly. “The pond heard a plip last night. Suspiciously button-shaped behavior.”

choices.label: Check around the pond
replies: You search the blue paper edge. Bandit finds one silver thread caught beneath a fold. “A clue! We are professionals now.”

choices.label: Ask the listening tree
replies: The tree rustles toward the pond. Bandit gasps. “The witness has spoken.”

opening: Bandit holds up the silver thread. It leads beneath the porch garden, where something gives a very guilty glint.

choices.label: Reach beneath the leaves
replies: Your fingers find a pearly paper button with one bent hole. Bandit hugs it, then remembers dignity. “Excellent finding.”

choices.label: Coax it out with a twig
replies: The button rolls free in a tiny circle. Bandit pounces with both little hands. “Captured without casualties.”

opening: “The moon is home,” Bandit says, “but one hole is creased. Every treasure deserves careful repairs.”

choices.label: Mend it with a tape sliver
replies: Together you smooth a near-invisible strip across the crease. Bandit tests it twice. “Stronger for having been found.”

choices.label: Keep the crease as a memory
replies: Bandit studies the crease. “Proof of adventure,” he decides. “That is also a kind of repair.”

opening: Bandit arrives wearing the moon button on a loop of thread. Beside it hangs a smaller button, warm as toast. “Collections need stories. This one is yours.”

choices.label: Accept the little sun button
replies: Bandit ties it carefully to your scrapbook. “Now our collections know each other.”

choices.label: Hang it in the clearing
replies: You hang the sun button where everyone can see it. Bandit’s eyes shine. “A public treasure. Very advanced friendship.”

opening: “You're in luck standing here, you know. This is bark-curl country — {{only-here:redwood-bark-curls}}.”
“Smell that? Redwoods. There's {{material:redwood-bark-curls}} to be had here, {{only-here:redwood-bark-curls}}.”

choices.label: How do I get {{material-short:redwood-bark-curls}}?
replies: “Not with your hands, and not with the little round-tipped pair. I hear you need {{tool-for:redwood-bark-curls}} to get through the bark.”

choices.label: What's it good for?
replies: “The nice decorative work. It's the handsome stuff — you don't waste it on a fence post.”

choices.label: Where else can I find it?
replies: “You can find it in {{found-in:redwood-bark-curls}}. Only off a living redwood, mind — you'll never find a pile of it lying about.”

opening: {{name}} is standing at the edge of the porch rail, toes over the line, tail rigged for launch. “I am going to jump it. The gap. Probably. Today, even.”

choices.label: Count them down
replies: You count three, two, one—{{name}} leaps, wobbles mid-air, and sticks the landing. “Did the ground notice? Tell me the ground noticed.”
“Three! Two! ONE!” {{name}} is airborne before you finish. The landing is ninety percent grace and ten percent rolling, which {{name}} declares was on purpose.

choices.label: Suggest a safety plan
replies: “A plan! Yes. Bold AND unbroken.” {{name}} paces out a landing zone, stacks two scraps as crash cushions, and jumps anyway. The cushions applaud.

opening: “I have half a question,” {{name}} says, holding it carefully, like it might spill. “It starts with 'why does the pond—' and then I lost the rest.”

choices.label: Help finish the question
replies: You wonder at it together until the missing half wanders in on its own. “Why does the pond ripple in circles! Thank you. I can sleep again, right after I find out.”

choices.label: Wonder out loud with them
replies: “Exactly! Wondering is better with a second brain.” You spend a while not knowing things, side by side. It is surprisingly filling.

opening: “Tonight. This clearing. One critter show,” {{name}} announces. “It is called 'The Leaf That Fell'. I need an audience of at least one. You qualify. Congratulations.”

choices.label: Take a front-row seat
replies: {{name}} performs the entire rise and fall of one brave leaf. There is a wind machine (a friend, blowing). At the end, {{name}} bows so deeply their nose touches the ground.
The show runs a full four minutes. {{name}} plays the leaf, the branch, the breeze, and one cloud who “brings texture”. By the falling scene, you are genuinely moved.

followUps.label: Call for an encore
replies: “An ENCORE?” {{name}} whispers, overcome. The second performance has twice the wind and three times the falling.

followUps.label: Give a glowing review
replies: “'Powerful,' you say. 'Grounded. Leaf-like.'” {{name}} writes every word on an imaginary poster.

choices.label: Offer to work the wind
replies: You are handed one (1) giant leaf and promoted to Weather. “On my cue,” {{name}} says, “make history.”

opening: {{name}} has built a tiny bed out of soft scraps. In it lies one wilted paper fern, drooping like a sad semicolon. “It got stepped on,” {{name}} whispers. “It needs quiet and good light.”

choices.label: Help set up the recovery bed
replies: You fold a watering can from a spare scrap and move the bed into a sunbeam with a view. “There,” {{name}} says. “Now it has a reason to stand back up.”

choices.label: Sit quietly with them
replies: You sit with {{name}} and the fern. Nobody says much. The fern, very slowly, unclenches one frond.

opening: “Keep your voice down,” {{name}} says, though you are outside and entirely alone. “I am going to move that garden stone two inches to the left. No one will know. Everyone will feel it.”

choices.label: Volunteer as lookout
replies: You watch the path. {{name}} shifts the stone with surgical ceremony. By afternoon, three critters say the clearing 'feels different'. Art.

choices.label: Suggest a worthier target
replies: “Worthier?” {{name}} gasps. You point at the pebble that has been hogging your favorite sitting spot all week. The pebble is relocated. “Justice,” {{name}} breathes, “but make it sneaky.”

opening: {{name}} waves you over with the urgency of a critter committing a crime. The crime is kindness. “I wrote a nice note for the neighbor. But if I deliver it, I will be SEEN.”

choices.label: Deliver it for them
replies: You slide the note under the porch gap while {{name}} watches from behind a fence post, thrilled beyond words. Later, the note is pinned up where everyone can see it.

choices.label: Help them practice saying it out loud
replies: “Hello. I. Like. Your. Garden.” Each word gets its own drumbeat of courage. By the tenth try, {{name}} is whispering it at full volume.

opening: {{name}} is lying in a sunbeam with the focused expression of a professional. “This one is top shelf,” they murmur. “Warm front, soft grain, ideal drift. But I believe there is a better one. Care to help me check?”

choices.label: Join the sunbeam tour
replies: You visit three candidate beams. {{name}} test-naps in each for quality control. The winner: a wide gold patch by the porch, rated 'fluffy'.

choices.label: Ask how the ratings work
replies: “Warmth is one star. Stillness is two stars. If a dust mote floats through it? That is the whole show.” {{name}} demonstrates by falling asleep mid-review.

opening: {{name}} pauses mid-step, suddenly very interested in being elsewhere. Then curiosity wins, the way it usually does. “...Hello. I have seen you around. You seem un-scary.”

choices.label: Say hello properly
replies: “Hello back.” {{name}} relaxes by one whole notch. “There. Now we are not strangers anymore. That was the hard part.”

choices.label: Offer a friendly wave
replies: You wave. {{name}} waves back with one careful paw, checking over both shoulders first. “That is how neighbors start,” they say, mostly to themselves.

opening: “Since we are friends now,” {{name}} says, suddenly bashful, “there is something I want to show you.” They open a secret fold and take out a small, well-polished treasure that has clearly been loved for a long time.

choices.label: Admire it properly
replies: You hold it carefully, like the honor it is. “It is better when someone else sees it too,” {{name}} admits. “That is why I showed you.”

choices.label: Share your own favorite thing
replies: {{name}} listens with both ears. “So that is yours. And this is mine.” They look pleased. “Now the treasures know each other, too.”

opening: “Follow me, and walk like a normal breeze,” {{name}} whispers. They lead you under a folded overhang to a hidden nook that is somehow exactly the right size for two. “This is my spot. I have never shown anyone. It needs a name, and I am terrible at names.”

choices.label: Help name the spot
replies: You toss ideas back and forth until one lands. “The Fold-Away,” {{name}} repeats, trying it on. “Yes. Official. I will make a tiny sign and everything.”

choices.label: Just sit there a while
replies: You sit in the good quiet. After a while {{name}} says, “You can come here anytime. That is what the spot was missing—a second someone who fits.”

opening: {{name}} is waiting at the exact spot you first met. “I saved you the good view,” they say, scooting over by exactly one critter-width.
{{name}} pats the ground beside them, twice, with great ceremony. “It is doing-nothing hour. You are officially invited.”
“I counted my favorite days,” {{name}} says as you settle in. “Most of them have you in them. Anyway. Sit.”

choices.label: Settle in for the quiet hour
replies: You watch the light move across the page together. No words needed. {{name}}'s slow blink is the whole conversation.
The breeze does the talking. Every so often {{name}} sighs the sigh of a critter whose life turned out good.
Time passes the way it should. Before you go, {{name}} says, “Same time, whenever. This is a standing invitation now.”

choices.label: Ask what their favorite memory is
replies: “The day I stopped being scared of you,” {{name}} says without hesitation. “Remember? I pretended I was busy. I was not busy. I was coming to find you.”

opening: “Good timing,” Chisel says, sliding over a fresh page ruled in tidy columns. “Job one for my helpers list: the mill needs a wind ledger. Height, gusts, drift. I can hold the ribbon, but I need someone to write what the wind is actually doing.”

choices.label: I'm your wind-writer
replies: “Knew you had it in you.” Chisel hands you a pencil sharpened to a reputable point. “Rule one of wind-writing: never chase the gust. Let it come to the page.”

choices.label: Why does a mill need wind data?
replies: “Paper timber curls in a crosswind. Trim tables drift. A mill that knows its wind is a mill that cuts straight.” He taps the ledger. “Also, I have always wanted a science.”

opening: Chisel has rigged a ribbon to a stick and a spool to a rock. “Instrumentation,” he explains, sounding extremely pleased about it. “We take readings from the high side of the page, where the wind introduces itself properly. Ready?”

choices.label: Take the high-side reading
replies: You hold the ribbon high while Chisel squints, mutters numbers, and writes in all caps. “Gust from the north, polite but firm. Excellent. That is a real entry in a real ledger.”

choices.label: Hold the ribbon steady
replies: The ribbon streams, dips, and loops. Chisel narrates every move like a sports announcer. “Little cyclone at the end there—bold choice by the wind. Noted.”

opening: “Now the part I am best at and like least,” Chisel admits. “Sitting still and writing it all neat.” The ledger is open. The pencil is ready. The wind, helpfully, keeps doing things.

choices.label: Write the neat copy
replies: You rule the columns; Chisel dictates. By the last entry the ledger is a thing of beauty. “Look at it,” he says softly. “Wind, but organized.”

choices.label: Add a wind drawing
replies: Chisel resists, then surrenders. The finished ledger now includes one diagram of a gust wearing a tiny hat. “Unscientific,” he declares. “It stays in forever.”

opening: Chisel has copied the ledger onto weatherproof stock and hung it by the cutter, next to a small hand-lettered plaque: MILL WIND LEDGER, EST. TODAY. “First science at the Wood Mill,” he says. “Wouldn't have pages one through nine without you.”

choices.label: Accept the Wind Medal
replies: He pins a hexagon of brass-look paper to your scrapbook, stamped with one proud spiral. “Official wind-writer, Wood Mill chapter. The role comes with responsibilities. Mostly snacking during readings.”

choices.label: Propose a daily reading time
replies: “A standing appointment? Now that is institution-quality thinking.” Chisel pencils WIND, WITH FRIEND into the corner of the ledger where appointments go.

opening: {{name}} looks like a critter with a math problem. “My acorn count keeps changing. Yesterday: forty. Today: forty-two. I counted twice! The acorns are doing something, and I intend to know what.”

choices.label: Offer to help recount
replies: “A second counter! The gold standard of counting.” {{name}} lines up the acorn ranks with military precision and hands you a pebble to mark your place. “No acorn left unturned. Or turned twice.”

choices.label: Ask for their leading theory
replies: “Theory one: acorns multiply when unobserved. Theory two: I cannot count. I have been avoiding theory two with great success until today.”

opening: The recount is underway. Piles everywhere, each one labeled with a tiny written number. “Thirty-eight, thirty-nine…” {{name}} freezes. “Wait. Who is PILE SEVEN? That pile was not there when we started.”

choices.label: Investigate pile seven
replies: Inside pile seven: a note. 'For the counter, from someone who appreciates organization.' {{name}} reads it four times. “The acorns have an ally. I am CHOOSING not to investigate further.”

choices.label: Count pile seven anyway
replies: “Four acorns. Round, excellent acorns.” {{name}} adds the total with trembling paws. “Forty-six. More than we started with. This is the greatest mystery of our time.”

opening: Mystery solved, mostly: a young squirrel had been leaving acorn gifts on the pile—“paying rent,” the little one said, “for living so close to a professional.” {{name}} has not stopped glowing since. “The census is complete. The answer was kindness. I am framing the ledger.”

choices.label: Help frame the ledger
replies: You press the counting page flat and fold a frame from kraft scraps. “Exhibit one,” {{name}} announces to the empty air. “The day mathematics failed and friendship succeeded.”

choices.label: Suggest leaving a gift back
replies: “Reciprocal acorns! Of course. An economy.” {{name}} selects the two roundest acorns for return delivery. “The rent situation here is about to get extremely fair.”

opening: {{name}} is crouched at the pond's edge, holding a leaf boat with both paws. “Race day,” they whisper. “The pond gets one good breeze an hour, and I have been practicing my launch. I need a rival. A friendly one. You.”

choices.label: Accept the rivalry
replies: “YES.” {{name}} hands you a pre-folded boat with a tiny painted stripe. “I made you the fast one by accident. You will never prove otherwise.”

choices.label: Ask about the course
replies: “Start line: that reed. Finish line: the shady fold. Hazards: one duck—no, that is a leaf. Unknown hazards: at least two.”

opening: The breeze is due. {{name}} lines both boats up at the reed start line, tongue out in concentration. “On three. One… two… three!” The pond does the rest.

choices.label: Launch your boat
replies: Your boat catches the breeze and rides the pond's soft ripple in a clean diagonal. {{name}}'s boat spins twice, bows to a lily pad, and finishes second—but with undeniable style points.

choices.label: Wait for the perfect gust
replies: You both hold, holding… then the gust arrives all at once. Both boats go skimming. It is a photo finish, if anyone had a camera, which no one does, so it is a story finish.

opening: “Champion's ceremony,” {{name}} announces, wearing a wreath of grass that is clearly sized for a much larger head. They hand you a tiny folded trophy. “The rules say the winner gets this. The rules also say the runner-up hosts the next regatta. I will begin planning.”

choices.label: Accept the tiny trophy
replies: The trophy is two pen-strokes tall and completely legitimate. You set it on your scrapbook edge, where it gleams. “Rematch whenever,” {{name}} says. “The pond is always in season.”

choices.label: Declare co-champions
replies: {{name}} gasps. “Shared victory? That is twice the trophy AND twice the bragging rights, which mathematically evens out to one each.” The wreath is split in two. It fits perfectly.

opening: “You are trustworthy,” the cat states, without preamble. “I can tell by your knees. There is a club. It meets after dark. There are snacks. This is not an invitation.” A slow blink. “Do you want in?”

choices.label: Say you're in
replies: “Good. Correct answer.” The cat writes your name on an invisible list with an invisible paw. “Orientation is whenever I say. Bring nothing. Want nothing. The snacks find you.”

choices.label: Ask what the club actually does
replies: “We walk. We sit on good surfaces. We find the snacks the day left behind: one seed here, a berry there. It is patrol work. It is important work.” A pause. “It is mostly sitting.”

opening: The moon is a paper circle with one corner peeled. The cat is waiting at the fence line, tail curled like a signature. “First patrol. Walk soft, judge quietly, and remember: anything shiny is a coincidence.”

choices.label: Walk the patrol route
replies: You check the porch gap (clear), the compost fold (one excellent berry, logged), and the sunny stone (sat upon, both of you, briefly). At the end the cat nods once. That is a standing ovation.

choices.label: Find a snack to log
replies: You spot a sun-warmed berry tucked by the fence post. The cat inspects it, declares it “club property,” and logs it in a ledger it definitely did not have a moment ago.

opening: At the fence line, the cat produces a small tin—where from is not explained—and pushes it toward you with one paw. “Membership dues, reversed. Members get snacks. This is the whole economy. Do not tell the raccoon.”

choices.label: Accept the membership tin
replies: Inside: two berries and one almond, each polished to a shine. The cat watches you pocket it, satisfied. “Club business is concluded. Same time, next moon. Bring your knees.”

choices.label: Leave something in the tin first
replies: The cat looks at what you added, then at you, then away—a cat's version of being moved. “The treasury has never had two of anything,” it says. “You may be going places, Club-wise.”

opening: “I am composing,” the bird announces from a low branch, “a duet. For bird and wind chime. The wind chime does not know yet, which is the hard part of any collaboration.” They look at you hopefully. “Will you be my rehearsal audience?”

choices.label: Accept the audience role
replies: “Excellent. You have the most important job: reacting.” The bird produces a concert program folded from a candy wrapper. Showtime is “soon, when the wind commits.”

choices.label: Offer to hum the chime's part
replies: The bird goes very still. “A stand-in chime. An UNDERSTUDY.” Feathers puff with excitement. “Rehearsal is now. Try to be metallic.”

opening: The branch has been arranged like a stage: two good acoustics leaves and a clear view of the wind chime, who hangs there, oblivious and glittering. The bird runs warm-up scales. “Cheep-cheep-cheeeep. Right. Places.”

choices.label: Perform the rehearsal
replies: The bird sings; you hum the chime's line. The real wind chime, caught up in the moment, rings once—perfectly on key. Both of you pretend to be calm about it.

choices.label: Conduct instead
replies: You conduct with a twig baton. The bird follows every gesture, including the ones you invent on the spot. “Dynamic!” they cry at your big finish. “I have never been so conducted.”

opening: Premiere day. A proper audience has gathered: two butterflies, a squirrel, and one beetle with strong opinions. The wind picks up right on cue. The bird looks at you, takes a breath, and begins.

choices.label: Cheer the premiere
replies: Bird and wind chime trade melodies until neither knows who is leading. The beetle cries. The squirrel applauds with an acorn against a trunk. “We did it,” the bird whispers, mid-bow. “The chime finally answered.”

choices.label: Host the after-party
replies: You gather seeds and berry slices on the best leaf in the forest. The wind chime rings politely whenever someone thanks it. “It IS a member,” the bird insists. “It gets a plate.”

opening: {{name}} unfurls a map made of petals, none of which are the same shape. “My life's work,” they explain. “A map of every good fold and bloom, from a flying height. It is missing three places. My wings stop where my courage does.”

choices.label: Offer to be their ground crew
replies: “A ground crew member! I fly, you confirm. Between us we will be an entire expedition.” {{name}} pins the petal map flat with four pebbles and taps a blank corner. “Start here. Probably. Maybe there.”

choices.label: Ask what makes a bloom good
replies: “Warmth in the petals, shade nearby for thinking, and a landing edge that does not argue with your wings.” {{name}} nods, satisfied with the list. “You learn these things. Or you crash gently a lot.”

opening: Expedition day. {{name}} spirals overhead, calling down landmarks while you navigate from below. “Big red fold! Small suspicious shadow! AN UNDOCUMENTED BLOOM—this is not a drill!”

choices.label: Mark the new bloom
replies: You press a petal from the new bloom onto the map's blank corner. {{name}} lands beside it, wings quivering. “Documented. My map has grown. I have grown, honestly.”

choices.label: Suggest naming the bloom
replies: “A name! For the map AND the legend.” You settle on The Second-Best Fold, which {{name}} insists is perfect, because now every explorer will want to find the first.

opening: The finished map hangs from a twig frame, petals and all. “Three blank corners to go,” {{name}} says, “but the map has learned to grow. That was the hard part. Maps do not finish. They get better.”

choices.label: Celebrate the cartographer
replies: You award the map a tiny gold seal (a very round crumb, applied ceremonially). {{name}} beams. “Official. When other butterflies ask, I will say: ground crew, excellent, one human, do not lose them.”

choices.label: Ask to join the next flight
replies: “Next season's survey? The team accepts.” {{name}} taps the remaining blank corners. “There is so much page left. That is my favorite thing about maps. And about friends, actually.”

opening: {{name}} holds two scraps up to the light, one in each paw, squinting like a jeweler. “Match these edges, and you learn where the paper weather came from. That one came from FAR away—the tear is homesick. I need a second opinion for the big survey.”

choices.label: Join the survey
replies: “Excellent. You take the tall pile, I take the interesting pile.” {{name}} sets a working table: twelve scraps, two suspect edges, one magnifying button (not needed, but professional).

choices.label: Ask how edge-matching works
replies: “Fibers remember. Hold two edges close, not touching, and feel for the pull—like magnets, but for paper.” {{name}} demonstrates: the scraps click together with a soft whisper. “See? Reunited.”

opening: The survey table now looks like a very small crime scene. “Nine matches,” {{name}} reports. “But these two refuse. Same color, same weight, OPPOSITE hearts.” They slide the quarreling scraps toward you. “You try. Fresh eyes.”

choices.label: Try the stubborn pair
replies: You rotate one scrap a quarter turn—and the edges settle together like a sigh. “Upside down the whole time,” {{name}} breathes. “Paper does not care which way is up. Noted for science.”

choices.label: Declare them a matched set
replies: “A SET! Of course!” {{name}} pairs them side by side, tears aligned. “They were never apart. They are a pair of bookmarks separated at birth.” The survey gains its first exhibit.

opening: The finished survey is pinned to a board: matched pairs, labeled origins, one scrap marked MYSTERY (KEEP). “We now know more about the paper weather than anyone,” {{name}} says, solemn. “This is a burden and a joy. Mostly a joy.”

choices.label: Help build a public exhibit
replies: You mount the board by the path where everyone can browse. {{name}} adds a sign: THE EDGE ARCHIVE. “Knowledge should be free,” they say, “and slightly shiny.”

choices.label: Ask about the mystery scrap
replies: “The one with no match? It stays on the board.” {{name}} taps it gently. “Every archive needs one open question. Otherwise, what would we do tomorrow?”

opening: “The forest gives twice,” {{name}} says. “Once in the branches, once underfoot. Most folk only look up.”

choices.label: What is up in the branches?
replies: “{{material:ribbonwood-sticks}} come loose and fall your way, and the redwoods keep {{material:redwood-bark-curls}} up high for anyone with {{tool-for:redwood-bark-curls}}.”

choices.label: And underfoot?
replies: “{{material:carbon-soil}} is right at the surface. {{material:graphite-cardstone}} sits deeper — a better shovel is what reaches it.”

choices.label: Why does the forest give so freely?
replies: “Because a forest is patient. Cut a little, wait a little, and it has already forgiven you.”

opening: “Palm country,” {{name}} says, shading their eyes. “The palms give {{material:palm-clippings}} and {{material:palm-fiber}}, {{only-here:palm-clippings}}.”

choices.label: How do I cut {{material-short:palm-clippings}}?
replies: “Trim the new growth with {{tool-for:palm-clippings}}. The palm barely notices, and it grows it all back.”

choices.label: What about the board here?
replies: “{{material:sunbaked-cardboard}} bakes flat in the sun and digs up easy. Honest building stock, and plenty of it.”

choices.label: Anything under the sand?
replies: “{{material:terracotta-pebbles}} rattle up out of the shallows. Pretty things, and warm to hold.”

opening: “Salvage rules,” {{name}} recites. “Pick up what lies loose, dig for what hides, and trust nothing that sparkles until you have inspected it twice.”

choices.label: What lies loose here?
replies: “{{material:ribbonwood-sticks}}, {{material:confetti-stones}}, {{material:sunbaked-cardboard}} — all of it free for the walking across.”

choices.label: What can I dig up?
replies: “{{material:graphite-cardstone}} sits deep here. You will want {{tool-for:graphite-cardstone}} if you mean to reach it.”

choices.label: How do I tell good scrap from bad?
replies: “There is no bad scrap. There is scrap you have not thought of a use for yet. Give it time. It will think of one.”

opening: “This is sowing country,” {{name}} says, flicking a seed packet with one toe. “Packets blow in and settle exactly where they would like to be planted. Kindly of them.”

choices.label: What grows well here?
replies: “{{material:raspberry-bush-seeds}} and {{material:crinkle-carrot-seeds}} both take to meadow paper. {{material:ribbon-corn-seeds}} too, if you have the patience.”

choices.label: Any good stones?
replies: “{{material:bluefold-pebbles}} and {{material:confetti-stones}} lie about in the open. Bluefolds are a meadow speciality — boast about those.”

choices.label: What is the soft stuff?
replies: “{{material:mossy-paper-fiber}}. Stuffing, weaving, quiet little nests. Everyone wants it and nobody picks enough.”

opening: “New around here?” {{name}} says. “Start simple. {{material:kraft-twigs}} and {{material:mossy-paper-fiber}} lie loose all over the clearing, free for the picking up.”

choices.label: And under the ground?
replies: “{{material:ochre-paperclay}} sits just beneath the surface. Any {{tool-for:ochre-paperclay}} turns it up, no skill required.”

choices.label: Anything to plant?
replies: “{{material:folded-cabbage-seeds}} turn up in the open. Slow eaters, but they fill a bed handsomely.”

choices.label: Thanks for the starter tips
replies: “Everyone starts with twigs. Nobody stays with twigs. Off you go.”

opening: “I have a project,” {{name}} says, and produces a page of plans that is mostly arrows. “To make {{material:bound-lumber}}, I need someone to fetch, and someone to lean on the maker. I have the maker. Are you the someone?”

choices.label: I am in. What do you need?
replies: “Raw wood, mostly. {{material:kraft-twigs}} and {{material:ribbonwood-sticks}} will do to start. Meet me back here, and we will feed the Thing Maker.”

choices.label: What is {{material:bound-lumber}} for?
replies: “Plans. Real ones. Bound lumber is wood that finally agrees with itself — walls, frames, things that stand up.” A pause. “I would like to build something that stands up.”

opening: “You brought materials!” {{name}} eyes the pile. “Feed the Thing Maker gently. It has moods, and the moods are load-bearing.”

choices.label: Feed the maker
replies: The scraps go in, and the Thing Maker works them over with a sound like a page turning twice. A neat length of {{material:bound-lumber}} comes out the far side. “It did the thing!” {{name}} whispers. “The thing it does!”

choices.label: Ask if the maker needs watching
replies: “Always. A maker is a friend with teeth.” {{name}} tracks every handle and lever, narrating softly. The {{material:bound-lumber}} that emerges is straight and proud.

opening: {{name}} stands over the finished {{material:bound-lumber}} with a plan in one paw and a hammer in the other, looking like a critter about to become a builder. “Last part. I need an extra pair of hands and a very small amount of courage.”

choices.label: Build the thing
replies: You hold, {{name}} hammers, and the two of you raise a small crooked shelf that is somehow perfect. {{name}} steps back. “It stands up,” they say, hushed. “I told you it would.”

choices.label: Suggest it needs a name first
replies: “A NAME.” {{name}} considers the shelf for a long moment. “The Leaning Tidy,” they declare. You write it on the plans in neat letters. The shelf, agreeably, leans.

opening: “Raw finds go in, refined things come out,” {{name}} says, patting the Thing Maker. “{{material:carbon-copy-shale}} and {{material:ochre-paperclay}} are the plain stock. Work them up, and you have better than you started with.”

choices.label: How does refining work?
replies: “Patiently. You gather what the ground gave you, arrange it the way the plan says, and the maker does the convincing. Nothing mystical about it. Mostly.”

choices.label: And {{material:bound-lumber}}?
replies: “The first real refine. Wood pressed until it holds a shape. Everything sturdy starts there.”

choices.label: Does it need a tool?
replies: “Only the maker, and a critter willing to wait for it. It is the waiting that thins the crowd.”

opening: “A better shovel is not a bigger shovel,” {{name}} says, tapping the ground. “It is permission. The surface layer is only the first page of what is under this one.”

choices.label: What does the next shovel reach?
replies: “{{tool:okayish-shovel}} takes on compact ground and steep banks. Denser paper, deeper down — the kind a real build wants.”

choices.label: And the best one?
replies: “{{tool:heavy-duty-shovel}} opens the deep seams. {{material:graphite-cardstone}}, mostly, and whatever the local geology is proudest of.”

choices.label: Why bother digging at all?
replies: “Because the ground is a scrapbook nobody has opened yet. You would be the first reader down there.”

opening: “Scissors are the gentlest tool,” {{name}} says, snipping at the air. “You do not take a tree. You borrow from it, and it grows the loan back.”

choices.label: What do the little scissors cut?
replies: “{{tool:kids-scissors}} take a small trim from ordinary trees. {{material:kraft-twigs}}, soft shoots — enough to keep you building.”

choices.label: So why upgrade?
replies: “Because {{tool:sturdy-scissors}} cut redwoods. {{material:redwood-bark-curls}} exist nowhere a lighter pair can reach. That is the whole ladder.”

choices.label: The trees do not mind?
replies: “Trees here are patient and renewable. Cut well, wait a little, come back. The forest keeps its own accounts.”

opening: “Building is just convincing paper to hold still,” {{name}} says, brandishing a hammer. “The trick is having a hammer polite enough to ask.”

choices.label: What can I build first?
replies: “{{tool:squeaky-hammer}} places the little pieces you already know how to make. Small things, honest things, a shelf for a friend.”

choices.label: What unlocks next?
replies: “{{tool:basic-mallet}}, and then {{tool:standard-hammer}}, take on bigger plans as they arrive — real frames, bound-lumber work, things that outlast the afternoon.”

choices.label: Can I take things apart?
replies: “Every join comes back open if you ask it nicely. A build you can unbuild is a build you can learn from.”

opening: {{name}} fidgets with the corner of a paper, then holds it out. “I trust you with this,” they say, which lands heavier than the paper does. “It is a list. Small things. Will you help?”

choices.label: Of course. What is on the list?
replies: “Three things: a little {{material:mossy-paper-fiber}}, a careful walk, and no questions until the end.” {{name}} smiles. “You already did the hard one. Come back when you have the fiber.”

choices.label: Why me?
replies: “Because you come back,” {{name}} says simply. “Most things do not. You do. That is a whole qualification.”

opening: {{name}} is waiting exactly where they said. The list is folded small in their paw. “No questions till the end,” they remind you. “Ready?”

choices.label: Hand over the fiber
replies: The walk is long, the fiber is soft, and the questions hold until the very end. {{name}} tucks the bundle away like treasure. “Thank you for coming back,” they say. It is the whole reward. It is enough.

choices.label: Ask one question early
replies: “One,” {{name}} allows. You spend it on something kind. They answer, then smile. “Good question. Now walk, and I will tell you the rest at the end.”

opening: “I keep a box of things I remember,” {{name}} says, sliding a folded carton into view. “Not objects. Moments. You are in it more than once.”

choices.label: Which moments?
replies: “The day you first said hello. The day you ‘happened’ to walk past three times.” {{name}} counts on their toes. “That is two. I am saving room for more.”

followUps.label: Add this one to the box
replies: “Consider it added,” {{name}} says, folding the moment in carefully. “The box is getting full. Good problem to have.”

followUps.label: Ask to see inside
replies: The box is mostly light and a few soft scraps, each one a day. {{name}} closes it before you can be embarrassed. “Later,” they say, fond.

choices.label: Tell them you keep one too
replies: {{name}} goes still, then bright. “A matching box? We are doing the same hobby,” they say. “This is the best kind of duplicate.”

opening: “I have been thinking about homes,” {{name}} says. “Mine is here.” A pause. “Yours is—wherever you keep going. I would like to see it once, if that is allowed.”

choices.label: Come see it anytime
replies: {{name}} does not answer for a moment. When they do, their voice is very small and very sure. “Then I will,” they say. “Twice, maybe. To be thorough.”

choices.label: Why now?
replies: “Because being friends a long while changes a thing,” {{name}} says. “Now I want to know where you go when you leave. Not to follow. Just to picture it kindly.”

opening: “I want to build a bench where the path bends,” {{name}} announces, “and I want it to be a secret. So if you help, you have to help quietly.”

choices.label: I can be quiet
replies: “Excellent. I will fetch the pieces; you keep the plan. We meet at the bend, with {{material:kraft-twigs}} and exactly no witnesses.”

choices.label: Why secret?
replies: “Because a bench that appears by surprise belongs to everyone who finds it,” {{name}} says. “That is the best way to give something.”

opening: The path bends around a quiet corner, and {{name}} is already there, sitting on a pile of untidy materials and looking extremely guilty. “It is going worse than planned,” they whisper. “Help?”

choices.label: Help build the bench
replies: You hold, {{name}} taps, and the bench that appears at the bend is small and level and better than any plan deserved. “Nobody asked for it,” {{name}} says, delighted. “That makes it a gift.”

choices.label: Rescue the crooked leg first
replies: You straighten the culprit leg with a scrap folded into a shim. The bench settles, satisfied. “Engineering,” {{name}} breathes, as if it were a spell. “Thank you for the engineering.”

opening: “I watch this horizon every day,” {{name}} says from their post, “and I have decided I want company for the watch. Not help. Just company.”

choices.label: Join the watch
replies: You stand beside {{name}} as the light moves across the corrugated ridges. Neither of you spots anything. Both of you feel important.

followUps.label: Stay quiet and keep watching
replies: You keep watch without words until the light runs long. {{name}} leans, just slightly, into the quiet beside you.

followUps.label: Ask what happens if something comes
replies: “Then we deal with it,” {{name}} says calmly. “Together, which is the whole point of company.”

choices.label: What are you watching for?
replies: “Nothing, usually. But if something ever came, I would want to have been watching.” {{name}} rises onto their tail, serious. “That is the job. And now you are part of it.”

opening: {{name}} is cupping a palmful of {{material:folded-cabbage-seeds}}. “I planted these somewhere important and forgot where. Help me reason it out?”

choices.label: Reason it out together
replies: You retrace the morning: the cool patch, the good light, the spot with the nicest view. “There!” {{name}} says, and off you both go to find a tiny green row already coming up. Found, by logic.

choices.label: Just walk until you find them
replies: You wander the forest floor until, inevitably, a small neat row of cabbage sprouts waves you over. “See?” {{name}} says. “The seeds wanted to be found. They are show-offs.”

“I promised I would think about {{material-short:redwood-bark-curls}}. Turns out you want {{tool-for:redwood-bark-curls}} for it, which I should have mentioned.”
“I asked around about {{material:graphite-cardstone}} since we spoke. It keeps to the deeper ground, and {{tool-for:graphite-cardstone}} reaches it.”
“Continuing our talk on materials — {{material:terracotta-pebbles}} lie loose in {{found-in:terracotta-pebbles}}. Warm little things. Go and see.”
harvest: “Since we were discussing what grows, here is the rest: {{material:raspberry-bush-seeds}} want a little room between the rows.”
“Continuing the harvest chat — {{material:crinkle-carrot-seeds}} come up quick, and the frilly tops are decorative even before the roots are useful.”
“Remember the garden talk? Note that {{material:paper-tomato-seeds}} do best on the hotter pages.”
“More on the harvest I promised: {{material:mend-me-seeds}} feed nobody, but they stitch a tired bed back into the sheet.”
“To finish the thought about food — {{material:ribbon-corn-seeds}} take their time, and they are worth every minute of it.”
wayfinding: “I mentioned a good walk last time, and I have walked it again since. From {{region}} the way bends about the way you remember.”
“Continuing where we left off: start from this {{biome}}, and the next page over always surprises people.”
“About the route I described — keep {{region}} behind you and the paper stays kind the whole way.”
“Since you asked about the way, here is the trick: follow the moss, then ignore the moss and follow the path.”
“The directions I gave you? Still good. Landmarks do not move unless the wind is showing off.”
fun: “I had another thought about {{region}}, seeing as you liked the last one.”
“More on this {{biome}}, as promised — it is even quieter in the early folds of the day.”
“Remember the thing I said about this place? It is still true. I checked twice.”
“A follow-up on the local scenery: today it did something new, and by new I mean it blinked.”
“I owe you the rest of the story about this {{biome}}. The rest is—well, it is lovely, mostly.”
place: “Last visit I told you about {{region}}. I went back to check, and it holds up.”
“Continuing our talk about this {{biome}}: every corner keeps a small secret, and I only know two of them.”
“About the place I described — the shady side is still the best side, even now.”
“I said I would keep an eye on {{region}}. Report: unchanged, pleasant, well worth the walk.”
“More on {{biome}}, as requested. It has a mood today, and the mood is gold.”
